title: Regulation of Mitophagy by the NSL Complex in Parkinson’s Disease
author: Karishma D’Sa

steps.title: Perform WPPINA Analysis
steps.instruction: Create a protein-protein interaction network based on Mendelian genes for PD (seeds) using data from databases within the IMEx consortium (https://www.imexconsortium.org/).

steps.title: Extract Core Network
steps.instruction: Topologically analyse the network to extract the core network (the most interconnected part), containing proteins/genes that can connect >60% of the initial seeds.

steps.title: Prioritize Complexes
steps.instruction: Obtain results of complex prioritization (neurocentric prioritization strategy) applied to the 2017 PD GWAS reported by Chang et al., 2017.

steps.title: Update Candidate Gene List
steps.instruction: Apply the same pipeline to the 2017 PD GWAS reported by Chang et al., 2017, to update the list of candidate genes.

steps.title: Extract Open Reading Frames (ORFs)
steps.instruction: Use the top single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) of the 2017 PD GWAS reported by Chang et al., 2017, to extract ORFs in cis-haplotypes defined by LD r2 ≥ 0.8.

steps.title: Identify Overlapping Proteins and Genes
steps.instruction: Match the extracted ORFs to the core network to identify overlapping proteins/genes in relevant/shared pathways.

steps.title: Perform Coloc Analysis
steps.instruction: Calculate posterior probabilities (PPH4) for each gene to test the hypothesis that the regulation of expression of a given gene and the risk for PD share a causal variant.

substeps.instruction: Consider genes with PPH4 ≥ 0.75 as having strong evidence for colocalization.
Generate plots using Gviz3, with gene and transcript details obtained from Ensembl v92 (https://www.ensembl.org/index.html).

steps.title: Identify Allele-Specific Expression (ASE) Sites
steps.instruction: Identify ASE sites by mapping RNA-seq data to personalised genomes as described by Guelfi et al, 2020.

substeps.instruction: Use RNA-seq data from 49 putamen and 35 substantia nigra tissue samples from the UK Brain Expression Consortium (https://ukbec.wordpress.com), obtained from neuropathologically normal individuals of European descent.
Test sites with greater than 15 reads in a sample for ASE.
Only consider sites present in non-overlapping genes and combine data from both tissues to increase power.
Mark ASE sites as those with a minimum false discovery rate (FDR) < 5% across samples.

steps.title: Perform Gene Ontology Analysis
steps.instruction: Evaluate the identified processes with Gene Ontology Biological Processes enrichment analysis (http://geneontology.org/).
